chapter: Pictures, Oliver, Armstrong and Fat Pichon
title: Red Batiste's saloon and its photographs of old musicians
summary: Arthur describes the saloon near the Dew Drop where Red Baptiste's wall of musician photos hung, including young Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: With a trumpet or just standing there?
He was playing trumpet then. He was just starting out to play, he just got out to whom, he was playing trumpet.
I can't remember seeing those pictures, I would have been seeing them.

This man died in this place close up, I don't know who could have gotten them pictures. Red Batiste. He had a saloon right up there across from the Doudrop and the next block coming this way from the Doudrop. Because I used to go up there, we used to go up there after a dance and eat breakfast in this place. And I used to stand up there a lot of time looking at all the old musicians up there. I mean he had a size card up there. That's been a power.
That's where the housing project is in there now or is it the Shakespeare Park? I can't think.

It's in that, you know where the Shakespeare Park is at? Yeah, I know the Doudrop. Well look, going uptown, where the Shakespeare Park starts, right from that corner coming down on that side of the bay. They got several saloons along that restaurant and things, but he was right in that section there.
Now whoever got that place, they might have gotten them pictures when he read Batiste Died. But I mean they had a lot of pictures of musicians and different folks.
Yeah, we all tried to check on something.

And Louis Armstrong's picture was in there when he was standing up. He was standing up with a cap on like that and he's got short pants on there. You know they were short pants at them times? Yeah. And he was playing trumpet then. And when I used to go see Louis Armstrong play for, they used to have parties up there, ten cents to go in. And he used to be- The ball and burning the pitch drives and things? No, this was little matinee parties in the yard. Yeah, and they'd sell punch and stuff like that. And he had a little young band, the young fellas all playing, he was blowing trumpet. He was playing plenty of trumpet then. He was nothing but a kid. I remember, and if you see that picture, that's just like him. But he was a boy, he has never changed from a kid. Now, if y'all would have had started this, of course y'all probably had started maybe in them times. I don't know, that's been- And Baptiste is dead now, what about-
Well, yeah, I've been asked, how long ago?

But Baptiste must be dead a good ten or twelve years now. About ten or twelve years ago. But if you could have got a hold of that, that, that, that, you had everything you wanted up on there. Maybe not everything, but you had a lot on there. Yeah.
Did he have any family that you know of? Who's that? Red Baptiste. I don't know any of his people.

I just knew him from having a place up there. And having a- Now, around in that section, if you could inquire around there, maybe somebody knows people. Somebody up there would know. I never lived uptown. The only way I went up there is after a dance, we would go up that way to get a breakfast in the morning. You see, and they used to sell, they used to serve some nice breakfast up in that section, you see. And we used to go up that way and eat. And then we would come back down in our section. But the bum up there, I never lived bum up there. Just mostly go up there in the mornings like that, after a dance and have breakfast, you see. From drinking, you know, he'd like to eat something, we'd go up there and have breakfast in the morning. And that's how I come, but I know the fellow Red Baptiste, I see him at football games too. But I don't know any of these people. I don't know who was his people up there.
It's possible this picture would be someplace here, I hope. Hard to run down any good pictures usually. Very few musicians kept scrapbooks.
